scene.label: Act 2, Scene 4
scene.title: SCENE IV. Another part of the Forest

content.text: Enter the empress' sons, Demetrius and Chiron with Lavinia, her hands cut off, and her tongue cut out, and ravished.

lines.text: So, now go tell, an if thy tongue can speak,
lines.plainText: So now go tell an if thy tongue can speak

lines.text: Who 'twas that cut thy tongue and ravished thee.
lines.plainText: Who 'twas that cut thy tongue and ravished thee

lines.text: Write down thy mind, bewray thy meaning so,
lines.plainText: Write down thy mind bewray thy meaning so

lines.text: An if thy stumps will let thee play the scribe.
lines.plainText: An if thy stumps will let thee play the scribe

lines.text: See how with signs and tokens she can scrowl.
lines.plainText: See how with signs and tokens she can scrowl

lines.text: Go home, call for sweet water, wash thy hands.
lines.plainText: Go home call for sweet water wash thy hands

lines.text: She hath no tongue to call, nor hands to wash;
lines.plainText: She hath no tongue to call nor hands to wash

lines.text: And so let's leave her to her silent walks.
lines.plainText: And so let's leave her to her silent walks

lines.text: An 'twere my cause, I should go hang myself.
lines.plainText: An 'twere my cause I should go hang myself

lines.text: If thou hadst hands to help thee knit the cord.
lines.plainText: If thou hadst hands to help thee knit the cord

lines.text: Who is this? My niece, that flies away so fast?
lines.plainText: Who is this My niece that flies away so fast

lines.text: Cousin, a word; where is your husband?
lines.plainText: Cousin a word where is your husband

lines.text: If I do dream, would all my wealth would wake me!
lines.plainText: If I do dream would all my wealth would wake me

lines.text: If I do wake, some planet strike me down,
lines.plainText: If I do wake some planet strike me down

lines.text: That I may slumber an eternal sleep!
lines.plainText: That I may slumber an eternal sleep

lines.text: Speak, gentle niece, what stern ungentle hands
lines.plainText: Speak gentle niece what stern ungentle hands

lines.text: Hath lopped and hewed and made thy body bare
lines.plainText: Hath lopped and hewed and made thy body bare

lines.text: Of her two branches, those sweet ornaments
lines.plainText: Of her two branches those sweet ornaments

lines.text: Whose circling shadows kings have sought to sleep in,
lines.plainText: Whose circling shadows kings have sought to sleep in

lines.text: And might not gain so great a happiness
lines.plainText: And might not gain so great a happiness

lines.text: As half thy love? Why dost not speak to me?
lines.plainText: As half thy love Why dost not speak to me

lines.text: Alas, a crimson river of warm blood,
lines.plainText: Alas a crimson river of warm blood

lines.text: Like to a bubbling fountain stirred with wind,
lines.plainText: Like to a bubbling fountain stirred with wind

lines.text: Doth rise and fall between thy rosed lips,
lines.plainText: Doth rise and fall between thy rosed lips

lines.text: Coming and going with thy honey breath.
lines.plainText: Coming and going with thy honey breath

lines.text: But sure some Tereus hath deflowered thee,
lines.plainText: But sure some Tereus hath deflowered thee

lines.text: And, lest thou shouldst detect him, cut thy tongue.
lines.plainText: And lest thou shouldst detect him cut thy tongue

lines.text: Ah, now thou turn'st away thy face for shame,
lines.plainText: Ah now thou turn'st away thy face for shame

lines.text: And notwithstanding all this loss of blood,
lines.plainText: And notwithstanding all this loss of blood

lines.text: As from a conduit with three issuing spouts,
lines.plainText: As from a conduit with three issuing spouts

lines.text: Yet do thy cheeks look red as Titan's face
lines.plainText: Yet do thy cheeks look red as Titan's face

lines.text: Blushing to be encountered with a cloud.
lines.plainText: Blushing to be encountered with a cloud

lines.text: Shall I speak for thee, shall I say 'tis so?
lines.plainText: Shall I speak for thee shall I say 'tis so

lines.text: O, that I knew thy heart, and knew the beast,
lines.plainText: O that I knew thy heart and knew the beast

lines.text: That I might rail at him to ease my mind.
lines.plainText: That I might rail at him to ease my mind

lines.text: Sorrow concealed, like an oven stopped,
lines.plainText: Sorrow concealed like an oven stopped

lines.text: Doth burn the heart to cinders where it is.
lines.plainText: Doth burn the heart to cinders where it is

lines.text: Fair Philomela, why she but lost her tongue,
lines.plainText: Fair Philomela why she but lost her tongue

lines.text: And in a tedious sampler sewed her mind;
lines.plainText: And in a tedious sampler sewed her mind

lines.text: But, lovely niece, that mean is cut from thee;
lines.plainText: But lovely niece that mean is cut from thee

lines.text: A craftier Tereus, cousin, hast thou met,
lines.plainText: A craftier Tereus cousin hast thou met

lines.text: And he hath cut those pretty fingers off
lines.plainText: And he hath cut those pretty fingers off

lines.text: That could have better sewed than Philomel.
lines.plainText: That could have better sewed than Philomel

lines.text: O, had the monster seen those lily hands
lines.plainText: O had the monster seen those lily hands

lines.text: Tremble like aspen leaves upon a lute,
lines.plainText: Tremble like aspen leaves upon a lute

lines.text: And make the silken strings delight to kiss them,
lines.plainText: And make the silken strings delight to kiss them

lines.text: He would not then have touched them for his life.
lines.plainText: He would not then have touched them for his life

lines.text: Or had he heard the heavenly harmony
lines.plainText: Or had he heard the heavenly harmony

lines.text: Which that sweet tongue hath made,
lines.plainText: Which that sweet tongue hath made

lines.text: He would have dropped his knife, and fell asleep,
lines.plainText: He would have dropped his knife and fell asleep

lines.text: As Cerberus at the Thracian poet's feet.
lines.plainText: As Cerberus at the Thracian poet's feet

lines.text: Come, let us go, and make thy father blind,
lines.plainText: Come let us go and make thy father blind

lines.text: For such a sight will blind a father's eye.
lines.plainText: For such a sight will blind a father's eye

lines.text: One hour's storm will drown the fragrant meads;
lines.plainText: One hour's storm will drown the fragrant meads

lines.text: What will whole months of tears thy father's eyes?
lines.plainText: What will whole months of tears thy father's eyes

lines.text: Do not draw back, for we will mourn with thee.
lines.plainText: Do not draw back for we will mourn with thee

lines.text: O, could our mourning ease thy misery!
lines.plainText: O could our mourning ease thy misery
